# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with Ollama backend (AMD GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://192.168.1.221:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "Ollama", port = 11434, info = "LLM backend (ROCM GPU)" },

```

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "ollama", "llm"]
}

  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"

  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

}

# Outputs

  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

  }
}

}

# Document Management Stack
# Paperless-ngx (OCR document management) + Stirling-PDF (PDF utilities)

name: documents

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Paperless-ngx - Document Management with OCR
  # ==========================================================================
  # Self-hosted document management with full-text search, auto-tagging,
  # and email consumption. All documents are OCR'd for searchability.
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:2.20.2
    container_name: paperless
    environment:
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-db
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev
      # Allow CSRF from both internal and public domains
      - PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,docs.rambtech.dev,localhost
      - PAPERLESS_CORS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_POLLING=60
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true
      - PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS=2
      - PAPERLESS_THREADS_PER_WORKER=2
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - paperless-data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - paperless-media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ./consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
      - ./export:/usr/src/paperless/export
    depends_on:
      paperless-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: paperless-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - paperless-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Redis - Cache/Broker for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-redis:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    volumes:
      - paperless-redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Stirling-PDF - PDF Manipulation Tools
  # ==========================================================================
  # Comprehensive PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, etc.
  # Stateless service - no persistent data needed.
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:2.1.3
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
      - SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
      - SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=en_US
      - UI_APPNAME=Stirling PDF
      - UI_HOMEDESCRIPTION=PDF tools for the homelab
      - METRICS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Training data for better OCR (optional)
      - stirling-tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
      # Custom configurations
      - stirling-configs:/configs
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-documents
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.24.1
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  paperless-data:
  paperless-media:
  paperless-pgdata:
  paperless-redis-data:
  stirling-tessdata:
  stirling-configs:
  portainer_agent_data:

# Document Management Stack
# Paperless-ngx (OCR document management) + Stirling-PDF (PDF utilities)

name: documents

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Paperless-ngx - Document Management with OCR
  # ==========================================================================
  # Self-hosted document management with full-text search, auto-tagging,
  # and email consumption. All documents are OCR'd for searchability.
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:2.20.2
    container_name: paperless
    environment:
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-db
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev
      # Allow CSRF from both internal and public domains
      - PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,docs.rambtech.dev,localhost,10.100.5.104
      - PAPERLESS_CORS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_POLLING=60
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true
      - PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS=2
      - PAPERLESS_THREADS_PER_WORKER=2
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - paperless-data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - paperless-media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ./consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
      - ./export:/usr/src/paperless/export
    depends_on:
      paperless-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: paperless-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - paperless-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Redis - Cache/Broker for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-redis:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    volumes:
      - paperless-redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Stirling-PDF - PDF Manipulation Tools
  # ==========================================================================
  # Comprehensive PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, etc.
  # Stateless service - no persistent data needed.
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:2.1.3
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
      - SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
      - SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=en_US
      - UI_APPNAME=Stirling PDF
      - UI_HOMEDESCRIPTION=PDF tools for the homelab
      - METRICS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Training data for better OCR (optional)
      - stirling-tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
      # Custom configurations
      - stirling-configs:/configs
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-documents
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.24.1
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  paperless-data:
  paperless-media:
  paperless-pgdata:
  paperless-redis-data:
  stirling-tessdata:
  stirling-configs:
  portainer_agent_data:

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.115.1
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-monitoring
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.5
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:
  portainer_agent_data:

# Homepage Services Configuration - ADMIN/INTERNAL
# Documentation: https://gethomepage.dev/en/configs/services/
#
# Widget API keys are loaded from environment variables via docker-compose.
# See: https://gethomepage.dev/configs/settings/#environment-variables
#
# Network: Services on 10.100.x.x container network, dual-NIC services also on 192.168.1.x

- Infrastructure:
    - Proxmox:
        href: "https://pve.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: Hypervisor management
        icon: proxmox.svg

    - Portainer:
        href: "https://portainer.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: Container management
        icon: portainer.svg
        widget:
            type: portainer
            url: "http://10.100.1.100:9000"
            env: 2
            key: "{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_PORTAINER_KEY}}"

    - Traefik:
        href: "https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: Reverse proxy & ingress
        icon: traefik.svg
        widget:
            type: traefik
            url: "https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev"

    - AdGuard Home:
        href: "https://dns.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: DNS server & ad blocking
        icon: adguard-home.svg
        widget:
            type: adguard
            url: "http://10.100.1.101:3000"
            username: "{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_USER}}"
            password: "{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_PASS}}"

- Services:
    - OpenWebUI:
        href: "https://openwebui.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: AI Chat Interface
        icon: "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-webui/open-webui/main/static/favicon.png"

    - Obsidian LiveSync:
        href: "https://obsidian.homelab.rambtech.dev/_utils"
        description: Obsidian note sync (CouchDB)
        icon: obsidian.svg

    - Immich:
        href: "https://photos.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: Photo management
        icon: immich.svg
        widget:
            type: immich
            url: "http://10.100.3.104:2283"
            key: "{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_IMMICH_KEY}}"
            version: 2
            fields:
                - photos
                - videos
                - storage

    - Paperless-ngx:
        href: "https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev"
        description: Document management

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.115.1
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-monitoring
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.5
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:
  portainer_agent_data:

# Prometheus Configuration
# Receives metrics from OpenTelemetry Collector and scrapes additional targets

global:
  scrape_interval: 30s
  evaluation_interval: 30s
  external_labels:
    monitor: 'homelab'

# Alerting configuration
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs:
        - targets:
            - alertmanager:9093

# Rule files for alerts
rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/alerts/*.yml

# Scrape configurations
scrape_configs:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Monitoring Stack Self-Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================

  # Prometheus self-monitoring
  - job_name: 'prometheus'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9090']

  # OpenTelemetry Collector metrics
  - job_name: 'otel-collector'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['otel-collector:8888']

  # Alertmanager metrics
  - job_name: 'alertmanager'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['alertmanager:9093']

  # Grafana metrics
  - job_name: 'grafana'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['grafana:3000']

  # ==========================================================================
  # Traefik Reverse Proxy Metrics
  # ==========================================================================
  - job_name: 'traefik'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.100.2.200:8082']
        labels:
          instance: 'traefik'
          lxc_id: '200'

  # ==========================================================================
  # AdGuard Home - DNS Metrics
  # Native Prometheus metrics not yet available in v0.107.70
  # TODO: Enable when PR #7937 is merged, or deploy adguard-exporter sidecar
  # https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome/pull/7937
  # ==========================================================================

  # ==========================================================================
  # Immich - Photo Management Metrics
  # Metrics pushed via OTEL to otel-collector (no scrape needed)
  # ==========================================================================

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Server Metrics
  # Requires: Prometheus plugin installed in Jellyfin

# Document Management Stack
# Paperless-ngx (OCR document management) + Stirling-PDF (PDF utilities)

name: documents

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Paperless-ngx - Document Management with OCR
  # ==========================================================================
  # Self-hosted document management with full-text search, auto-tagging,
  # and email consumption. All documents are OCR'd for searchability.
  paperless:
    image: ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:2.20.2
    container_name: paperless
    environment:
      - PAPERLESS_REDIS=redis://paperless-redis:6379
      - PAPERLESS_DBHOST=paperless-db
      - PAPERLESS_DBNAME=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBUSER=paperless
      - PAPERLESS_DBPASS=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY}
      - PAPERLESS_URL=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev
      # Allow CSRF from both internal and public domains
      - PAPERLESS_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,docs.rambtech.dev,localhost
      - PAPERLESS_CORS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=https://docs.homelab.rambtech.dev,https://docs.rambtech.dev
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      - PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      - PAPERLESS_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
      - PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE=eng
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_POLLING=60
      - PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true
      - PAPERLESS_TASK_WORKERS=2
      - PAPERLESS_THREADS_PER_WORKER=2
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:
      - paperless-data:/usr/src/paperless/data
      - paperless-media:/usr/src/paperless/media
      - ./consume:/usr/src/paperless/consume
      - ./export:/usr/src/paperless/export
    depends_on:
      paperless-db:
        condition: service_healthy
      paperless-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # PostgreSQL - Database for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    container_name: paperless-db
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=paperless
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_DB=paperless
    volumes:
      - paperless-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U paperless"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Redis - Cache/Broker for Paperless-ngx
  # ==========================================================================
  paperless-redis:
    image: redis:8.4-alpine
    container_name: paperless-redis
    volumes:
      - paperless-redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Stirling-PDF - PDF Manipulation Tools
  # ==========================================================================
  # Comprehensive PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, etc.
  # Stateless service - no persistent data needed.
  stirling-pdf:
    image: stirlingtools/stirling-pdf:2.1.4
    container_name: stirling-pdf
    environment:
      - DOCKER_ENABLE_SECURITY=false
      - SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=false
      - SYSTEM_DEFAULTLOCALE=en_US
      - UI_APPNAME=Stirling PDF
      - UI_HOMEDESCRIPTION=PDF tools for the homelab
      - METRICS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Training data for better OCR (optional)
      - stirling-tessdata:/usr/share/tessdata
      # Custom configurations
      - stirling-configs:/configs
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info/status || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-documents
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.6
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  paperless-data:
  paperless-media:
  paperless-pgdata:
  paperless-redis-data:
  stirling-tessdata:
  stirling-configs:
  portainer_agent_data:

# Jellyfin Media Server Stack
# Includes: Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, Jellystat + PostgreSQL

name: jellyfin

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Streaming Server
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyfin:
    image: jellyfin/jellyfin:10.11.5
    container_name: jellyfin
    user: 1000:1000
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    ports:
      - "8096:8096"
    volumes:
      - jellyfin-config:/config
      - jellyfin-cache:/cache
      - /data/library:/data/library:ro
    # AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding (VA-API)
    group_add:
      - "44"   # video group for GPU access
      - "104"  # render group for GPU access
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyseerr - Media Request Management (Overseerr fork for Jellyfin)
  # ==========================================================================
  jellyseerr:
    image: fallenbagel/jellyseerr:2.7.3
    container_name: jellyseerr
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
    ports:
      - "5055:5055"
    volumes:
      - jellyseerr-config:/app/config
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellystat - Statistics and Analytics for Jellyfin
  # ==========================================================================
  jellystat:
    image: cyfershepard/jellystat:1.1.6
    container_name: jellystat
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - POSTGRES_USER=jellystat
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD}
      - POSTGRES_IP=jellystat-db
      - POSTGRES_PORT=5432
      - JWT_SECRET=${JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET}
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - jellystat-data:/app/backend/backup-data
    depends_on:
      jellystat-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Diun (Docker Image Update Notifier) and monitoring multiple hosts with remote Docker SSH:

## Diun - Docker Image Update Notifier

Diun is a CLI application written in Go and delivered as a single executable (and a Docker image) to receive notifications when a Docker image is updated on a Docker registry.

### Key Features

With Go, this can be done with an independent binary distribution across all platforms and architectures that Go supports. This support includes Linux, macOS, and Windows, on architectures like amd64, i386, ARM, PowerPC, and others.(no content)It will scan your local Docker instance and compare all images with the repository to get info if there is an update or not. As a great notification system, it offers multiple ways to get that information back to you: Amqp, Discord, Gotify, Mail, Matrix, MQTT, Pushover, Rocket.Chat, Script, Slack, Teams, Telegram, Webhook.

### Multiple Hosts / Remote Docker

There was a request to implement remote monitoring for a few remote docker instances from one Diun - for example listing them and giving a name with IP via a config file or using variables like REMOTE_HOST1_HOST and REMOTE_HOST1_NAME. The question asked whether such functionality would require a lot of effort and is impossible now.(no content)DIUN supports multiple monitoring configurations (Providers): Docker - analyzes images of running containers on Docker hosts and checks for updates; Podman - similar to Docker, requires Podman to be started as a service.

### Running on Multiple Hosts

If you've got more than one box with Diun on, you'll probably struggle to work out which is sending you notifications if you're relying on randomly generated hostnames. Setting the container hostname is recommended.

The common approach appears to be running a separate Diun instance on each Docker host rather than connecting to multiple remote hosts from a single Diun instance. One user reported using crazy-max/diun starting in July 2024 to keep track of new releases for docker images. It will on a daily schedule look at the repository on Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry, etc and see if there is a new tag/image available.

### Documentation

Documentation can be found at https://crazymax.dev/diun/

For connecting to remote Docker hosts via SSH, you would typically need to configure the Docker provider to connect to a remote Docker socket, though the search results don't show explicit SSH configuration examples. The GitHub issue (#263) suggests this multi-host feature was requested but may not be fully implemented in a single-instance configuration.

# Diun Docker Connection Methods

Based on the documentation, Diun connects to Docker through the **`endpoint`** configuration option, which specifies the server address.

## Connection Configuration

The primary setting is:

**`endpoint`**: "Server address to connect to. Local if empty."

### Example Configuration

The documentation shows a local connection example:
```
providers:
  docker:
    endpoint: "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
```

## Remote Connection Support

While the documentation mentions an `endpoint` parameter that accepts "server address," it does not explicitly detail SSH or TCP remote connection examples. The configuration appears flexible enough to support remote hosts through the endpoint parameter, but specific remote connection syntax (SSH URIs, TCP addresses, etc.) is not documented in this provided content.

## Related Configuration Options

Additional connection settings include:
- **`apiVersion`**: Override client version
- **`tlsCertsPath`**: Path to TLS certificates
- **`tlsVerify`**: Enable/disable certificate verification (default: true)

The presence of TLS certificate options suggests support for secure remote connections, though explicit remote host examples aren't provided in this documentation excerpt.

Based on my research, **Diun does support remote Docker hosts** via TCP endpoints with TLS, but not natively via SSH. The common approach for multi-host setups is:

**Option A: Run Diun on each LXC** (recommended for your setup)
- Each LXC runs its own Diun instance monitoring local containers
- All instances send notifications to your central ntfy server
- Simple, no remote Docker configuration needed

**Option B: Single Diun with remote Docker over TCP+TLS**
- Requires exposing Docker API on each LXC (security concern)
- More complex setup

Given your setup with Portainer Edge Agents already connecting to a central Portainer, **Option A** is cleaner - run Diun on each LXC alongside the Portainer Edge Agent, all sending notifications to ntfy.

However, there's an even simpler approach: **Just add ntfy notifications to your existing Watchtower** on the Portainer LXC. Watchtower supports notifications via webhook/shoutrrr which can post to ntfy.

Which approach would you prefer?
1. **Add ntfy notifications to existing Watchtower** (simplest - just add config)
2. **Replace Watchtower with Diun on Portainer LXC** (cleaner for monitor-only)
3. **Deploy Diun to all LXCs** (comprehensive - monitors all hosts)

Sources:
- [Diun GitHub](https://github.com/crazy-max/diun)
- [Diun Documentation](https://crazymax.dev/diun/)
- [Multi-host discussion](https://github.com/crazy-max/diun/issues/263)
wait i dont understand option 2

Let me clarify Option 2:

**Option 2: Replace Watchtower with Diun on Portainer LXC**

Currently on LXC 100 (Portainer), you have:
- Portainer CE (container management UI)
- Watchtower (monitors for updates but has no notifications configured)

With Option 2, you would:
- Remove Watchtower from that LXC
- Add Diun instead
- Diun would only monitor the containers **on that single LXC** (portainer + watchtower itself)

**The problem**: Diun on LXC 100 would only see containers running on LXC 100. It wouldn't see containers on your other LXCs (jellyfin, documents, monitoring, etc.) unless you either:
- Expose Docker API over TCP on each LXC (security risk)
- Run Diun on each LXC separately (Option 3)

**So in your case**, the practical options are really:

1. **Add ntfy notifications to existing Watchtower** - Quick fix, but only monitors LXC 100
2. **Deploy Diun to all LXCs** - Each LXC monitors its own containers, all notify to ntfy

Since you want to monitor **all** Docker hosts, **Option 3 (Diun on all LXCs)** is actually the right approach. Each LXC would have a small Diun container that monitors local containers and sends notifications to your central ntfy server.

Yes, that's right. With this approach, every LXC would have two common containers:

**Alternative: Centralized Diun with registry watching**

- Run a single Diun instance on the monitoring LXC (500)
- Configure it to watch specific images from registries (Docker Hub, GHCR, etc.) rather than scanning running containers

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|
| **Diun on each LXC** | Auto-discovers containers, no manual image list | More containers to manage, duplicated config |
| **Centralized Diun** | Single instance, easier to manage | Must manually maintain image list, won't catch new containers automatically |

That's a great architectural question. Here are common "sidecar" containers that often run on every Docker host:

**Currently common:**
1. **Portainer Edge Agent** - container management

**Potential future additions:**
2. **Diun** - image update notifications
3. **Log agent** - Promtail, Fluent Bit, or Vector for centralized logging (to Loki/Elasticsearch)
4. **Node exporter** - Prometheus metrics for host-level monitoring (CPU, memory, disk)
5. **cAdvisor** - Container-level metrics for Prometheus
6. **Fail2ban agent** - if you centralize intrusion detection
7. **Backup agent** - for container volume backups

**Separating into its own compose file makes sense:**

```
/config/
├── docker-compose.yml          # Application services
├── infrastructure.yml          # Common infrastructure agents
│   ├── portainer-edge-agent
│   ├── diun
│   ├── promtail (future)
│   └── node-exporter (future)
```

- Clean separation of concerns
- Can update infrastructure agents across all LXCs without touching app configs
- Potentially manage infrastructure.yml via a shared template in tofu modules

whats node-exporter?

**Node Exporter** is a Prometheus exporter that collects **host-level metrics** - things about the machine itself rather than the containers running on it:

- **CPU** - usage, load average, per-core stats
- **Memory** - used, free, cached, buffers
- **Disk** - usage, I/O, read/write speeds
- **Network** - bandwidth, packets, errors
- **Filesystem** - mount points, space
- **System** - uptime, kernel info

Currently your Prometheus setup scrapes **container metrics** (from Traefik, Grafana, etc.), but you don't have visibility into the underlying LXC host resources.

With Node Exporter on each LXC, you could create Grafana dashboards showing:
- Which LXC is running low on disk
- CPU usage across all hosts
- Memory pressure alerts
- Network throughput per host

**However**, for your setup there's a consideration: Your LXCs are containers themselves running on Proxmox. You might get better visibility by:

1. **Node Exporter on Proxmox host** - monitors the actual hardware
2. **Proxmox's built-in metrics** - you already have OTEL pushing Proxmox metrics

So Node Exporter on each LXC would show you per-LXC resource usage, which could still be useful for capacity planning (e.g., "the media-management LXC needs more RAM").

Want me to note this as a potential future addition in the infrastructure task, or skip it since Proxmox metrics may be sufficient?

Yes, you have a few options:

**1. Grafana Dashboard (recommended)**

You can create a Grafana dashboard that shows Glances-like stats. Since you already have:
- **Proxmox metrics via OTEL** - host-level CPU, memory, disk, network
- **Traefik metrics** - request rates, response times
- **Container metrics** from various apps

You could build a single "Overview" dashboard in Grafana showing all LXCs at a glance.

**2. Homepage Widgets**

Homepage (which you're already using) supports widgets for:
- **Glances** - you already have this on dashboards LXC
- **Prometheus** - can show custom queries
- **Grafana** - can embed panels

**3. Glances on Proxmox Host**

Run Glances directly on the Proxmox host (not in a container) to monitor the actual hardware. Your current Glances on dashboards LXC only sees that LXC's resources.

**What would be most useful for you?**

| Option | Shows | Effort |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Grafana "Overview" dashboard | All LXCs, Proxmox host, historical data | Medium - need to build dashboard |
| Glances on Proxmox | Real hardware stats | Low - just install |
| Homepage with Prometheus widget | Key metrics on homepage | Low - add widget config |

The Grafana approach gives you the richest view since you can combine Proxmox host metrics + per-LXC stats + container metrics all in one place with alerting.

Want me to create a task to build a Grafana overview dashboard, or would you prefer one of the other options?
so running a node-exporter on LXCs then would make sense right?

Yes, it would make sense if you want per-LXC visibility in Grafana. Here's why:

**What you'd get with Node Exporter on each LXC:**
- CPU/memory/disk usage per LXC
- See which LXC is resource-constrained
- Historical trends (Grafana can show "jellyfin LXC memory grew 20% this month")
- Alerting ("documents LXC disk > 80%")

**How it fits together:**

```
Proxmox Host (via OTEL)     →  Overall hardware health
     ↓
LXC Node Exporters          →  Per-LXC resource usage  
     ↓
Container metrics           →  Per-app stats (Jellyfin streams, Immich photos, etc.)
```

This gives you three layers of observability, and you could build a Grafana dashboard that shows all LXCs in a grid - similar to Glances but for your entire homelab.

**So the plan could be:**

1. **Infrastructure compose refactor** - Separate Portainer Edge Agent into `infrastructure.yml`
2. **Add Diun** - Container update notifications
3. **Add Node Exporter** - Host metrics per LXC
4. **Grafana Overview Dashboard** - Visualize all LXCs at a glance

All three (Portainer Agent, Diun, Node Exporter) would live in `infrastructure.yml` on each LXC.

yes another thing i would like to revisit is how we manage docker compose yamls - any change in those yaml files would most likely result in us restarting containers for atleast updating them. given how we are clubbing along with the rest of the files and using filesync provider, we cant really update them forcing us to only do that via ssh'ing into the container manually.
The way i see it we have 3 options:
1. we can reintroduce the remote-docker-compose(https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/terraform-provider-remote-docker-compose-file) provider that can provide us hooks into recreating containers directly
2. update our filesync provider to give us post-actions that can do this for us using the same file-sync-provider we currently use
3. use null-provider to remote-exec the docker container restarts

the only thing i am not sure of though is once we restart the containers, how do we monitor if the containers actually came back up correctly in a centralized way

Good analysis. Let me add my thoughts on each option:

**Option 1: remote-docker-compose provider**
- Pros: Purpose-built, clean integration
- Cons: Another provider to maintain, you'd need to keep it updated

**Option 2: filesync provider with post-actions**
- Pros: Single provider does both file sync + restart
- Cons: Requires modifying the provider, mixing concerns (file sync ≠ container orchestration)

**Option 3: null_resource with remote-exec**
- Pros: Works today, no provider changes needed
- Cons: Always runs on every apply (or needs triggers), clunky

**My recommendation: Option 1 (remote-docker-compose)**

It's the cleanest separation of concerns:
- `filesync` → manages files
- `remote-docker-compose` → manages container lifecycle

For the **health monitoring** question, you could:

1. **Immediate feedback** - The provider could wait for containers to be healthy (check `docker compose ps` for health status)
2. **Post-apply verification** - Add a `null_resource` that queries container health after apply
3. **External monitoring** - Rely on Uptime Kuma / Prometheus alerts to catch failures

A robust flow would be:
```
filesync (deploy files) 
    → remote-docker-compose (pull + up -d)
        → wait for healthy status (built into provider)
            → fail terraform if unhealthy after timeout
```

Want me to create a task to explore reviving the remote-docker-compose provider with health checking built in?

yes! my problem with `fail terraform if unhealthy after timeout` is that all both these providers i created, was with the understanding that the providers will explicitly not manage container lifecycle to maintain terraform best practices and not complicate the provider by being a docker container manager. The scope of those 2 providers is thus limited to file management. 
maybe we cna use our current observability tools like graphana and uptime kuma to resolve the observability issue

That's a good principle - keeping the providers focused on file management and not trying to make them container orchestrators.

So the approach would be:

**Providers (file management only):**
- `filesync` → deploy files
- `remote-docker-compose` → deploy compose file + trigger `docker compose up -d` (fire and forget)

**Observability (external verification):**
- **Uptime Kuma** → already monitors all service endpoints, will alert if something goes down
- **Grafana/Prometheus** → can alert on container health metrics
- **ntfy** → receives alerts from both

The flow becomes:
```
tofu apply
    → filesync deploys configs
    → remote-docker-compose triggers `docker compose pull && up -d`
    → apply completes (doesn't wait for health)

Meanwhile (async):
    → Uptime Kuma detects service down → ntfy alert
    → You investigate and fix
```

This keeps the providers simple and leverages your existing monitoring stack for the "did it actually work" verification.

The tradeoff is you won't get immediate feedback in the terraform output if something failed, but you'll know within minutes via your alerting.

Want me to create a task for reviving the remote-docker-compose provider with this simpler scope?
can diun help us here in any way? maybe it can keep track of and notify if a container failed to come up directly?

Diun is specifically for **image update notifications** - it checks registries for new image versions, not container health. So it won't help with "did this container start successfully."

However, there are a couple of tools that *could* fill this gap:

**1. Docker Events → ntfy**
A lightweight container that listens to Docker events (start, stop, die, health_status) and forwards them to ntfy:

```yaml
docker-events-notifier:
  image: containrrr/shoutrrr  # or a simple script
  # Listens to: docker events --filter 'event=die' --filter 'event=health_status'
  # Sends to ntfy when container dies or becomes unhealthy
```

**2. Autoheal** (proactive restart)
Monitors container health and auto-restarts unhealthy containers:
```yaml
autoheal:
  image: willfarrell/autoheal
  volumes:
    - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
  environment:
    - AUTOHEAL_CONTAINER_LABEL=all
```

**3. Your existing Uptime Kuma**
Already monitors HTTP endpoints - if a service doesn't come up, you'll get an alert.

The gap is really: **"container crashed but service never came up"** vs **"service came up but is slow/degraded"**

For your use case, I'd suggest:
- **Uptime Kuma** handles "is the service reachable" (already have this)
- **Docker events → ntfy** could notify on container crashes/restarts (new)

This would be a small addition to the infrastructure stack epic. Want me to add it as a subtask?

ooohh i think i really like that docker events approach! yes lets add that to the infrastructure epic. Also add the task to move to remote-docker-compose provider so that we can do that docker-compose up using the provider itself rather than manually

Description:
Deploy common infrastructure containers to all Docker LXCs for observability and monitoring.

## Goal
Separate infrastructure/sidecar containers from application containers by creating a dedicated `infrastructure.yml` compose file on each LXC.

## Infrastructure Stack Components
1. **Portainer Edge Agent** (existing) - Container management

/config/
├── docker-compose.yml      # Application services
├── infrastructure.yml      # Common infrastructure agents
```

## Implementation Steps
1. Refactor docker-lxc module to support infrastructure.yml
2. Move Portainer Edge Agent from app compose to infrastructure.yml
3. Add Diun with ntfy notifications
4. Add Node Exporter with Prometheus scrape targets
5. Build Grafana 'LXC Overview' dashboard

- portainer (100), network-services (101)
- traefik (200), dashboards (201), authelia (202)
- immich (304)
- jellyfin (401), media-management (402)
- monitoring (500), openwebui (501), n8n (502), obsidian-sync (503), documents (504)

## Benefits
- Clean separation of app vs infrastructure concerns
- Centralized update notifications via Diun → ntfy
- Per-LXC resource visibility in Grafana
- Easier to add future infrastructure agents (log collectors, etc.)

bd update proxmox-homelab-mcd.1 --description="Add a docker-events-notifier container to the infrastructure stack that monitors Docker events and sends notifications to ntfy when containers crash, restart unexpectedly, or fail to start.

## Why
- Diun only monitors image updates, not container health
- Need real-time visibility into container crashes across all LXCs
- Complements Uptime Kuma (which monitors HTTP endpoints) with container-level events

## Implementation
1. Create lightweight container that subscribes to Docker events API
2. Filter for relevant events: die, kill, restart, oom
3. Forward notifications to ntfy homelab-alerts topic
4. Include container name, event type, and LXC identifier in message

## Reference
- Docker events API: https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.43/#tag/System/operation/SystemEvents
- Can be a simple Python script similar to ntfy-discord-forwarder pattern"

bd update proxmox-homelab-mcd.2 --description="Replace filesync provider with remote-docker-compose provider for managing Docker Compose deployments via tofu.

## Why
- Currently using filesync provider which only syncs files, not container lifecycle
- Need to run 'docker compose up -d' after file changes
- Manual SSH to restart containers is error-prone and doesn't scale

## Implementation
1. Use or extend remote-docker-compose provider
2. Provider should:
   - Sync docker-compose files (like filesync)
   - Execute 'docker compose up -d --remove-orphans' after changes
   - NOT manage container health (leave that to observability tools)
3. Keep provider focused on file management + restart trigger
4. Rely on docker-events-notifier + Uptime Kuma for health visibility

## Design Philosophy
- Providers manage file state and trigger restarts
- External observability (Uptime Kuma, Grafana, docker-events) monitors health
- Clear separation of concerns"

 {"id":"proxmox-homelab-4a1","title":"Epic: Convert LXC containers to unprivileged mode","description":"CRITICAL SECURITY: Convert privileged LXC containers to unprivileged mode where possible.

## Background
All 12 LXC containers currently run with unprivileged=false. Unprivileged containers provide better security - container UID 0 maps to unprivileged user on host.

## Requirements for Unprivileged Docker-in-LXC
- unprivileged = true
- enable_nesting = true (required for Docker namespaces)
- enable_keyctl = true (required for kernel key operations)
- enable_fuse = false (set true only if using ZFS storage)

## CVE-2025-52881 Note
Recent containerd update broke Docker in LXC. Ensure lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2 on Proxmox host.

## Migration Strategy
- Convert each LXC independently (child issues)
- Test thoroughly before moving to next
- Some LXCs may need to stay privileged
- Document any issues encountered

+{"id":"proxmox-homelab-mcd","title":"LXC Infrastructure Stack: Observability & Monitoring","description":"Deploy common infrastructure containers to all Docker LXCs for observability and monitoring.

## Goal
Separate infrastructure/sidecar containers from application containers by creating a dedicated `infrastructure.yml` compose file on each LXC.

## Infrastructure Stack Components
1. **Portainer Edge Agent** (existing) - Container management
2. **Diun** - Docker image update notifications → ntfy
3. **Node Exporter** - Host-level metrics for Prometheus

## Architecture
```
/config/
├── docker-compose.yml      # Application services
├── infrastructure.yml      # Common infrastructure agents
```

## Implementation Steps
1. Refactor docker-lxc module to support infrastructure.yml
2. Move Portainer Edge Agent from app compose to infrastructure.yml
3. Add Diun with ntfy notifications
4. Add Node Exporter with Prometheus scrape targets
5. Build Grafana 'LXC Overview' dashboard

## LXCs to update
- portainer (100), network-services (101)
- traefik (200), dashboards (201), authelia (202)
- immich (304)
- jellyfin (401), media-management (402)
- monitoring (500), openwebui (501), n8n (502), obsidian-sync (503), documents (504)

## Benefits
- Clean separation of app vs infrastructure concerns
- Centralized update notifications via Diun → ntfy
- Per-LXC resource visibility in Grafana
- Easier to add future infrastructure agents (log collectors, etc.)","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"epic","created_at":"2025-12-17T22:38:08.857781-05:00","updated_at":"2025-12-17T22:38:08.857781-05:00"}
+{"id":"proxmox-homelab-mcd.1","title":"Docker Events Notifier: Container crash/restart notifications to ntfy","description":"Add a docker-events-notifier container to the infrastructure stack that monitors Docker events and sends notifications to ntfy when containers crash, restart unexpectedly, or fail to start.

## Why
- Diun only monitors image updates, not container health
- Need real-time visibility into container crashes across all LXCs
- Complements Uptime Kuma (which monitors HTTP endpoints) with container-level events

## Implementation
1. Create lightweight container that subscribes to Docker events API
2. Filter for relevant events: die, kill, restart, oom
3. Forward notifications to ntfy homelab-alerts topic
4. Include container name, event type, and LXC identifier in message

## Reference
- Docker events API: https://docs.docker.com/engine/api/v1.43/#tag/System/operation/SystemEvents

+{"id":"proxmox-homelab-mcd.2","title":"Integrate remote-docker-compose provider for automated container lifecycle","description":"Replace filesync provider with remote-docker-compose provider for managing Docker Compose deployments via tofu.

## Why
- Currently using filesync provider which only syncs files, not container lifecycle
- Need to run 'docker compose up -d' after file changes
- Manual SSH to restart containers is error-prone and doesn't scale

## Implementation
1. Use or extend remote-docker-compose provider
2. Provider should:
   - Sync docker-compose files (like filesync)
   - Execute 'docker compose up -d --remove-orphans' after changes
   - NOT manage container health (leave that to observability tools)
3. Keep provider focused on file management + restart trigger
4. Rely on docker-events-notifier + Uptime Kuma for health visibility

## Design Philosophy
- Providers manage file state and trigger restarts
- External observability (Uptime Kuma, Grafana, docker-events) monitors health

## Migration Strategy
- Convert each LXC independently (child issues)
- Test thoroughly before moving to next
- Some LXCs may need to stay privileged
- Document any issues encountered

Perfect! I have gathered comprehensive information. Now let me create a detailed report on the homelab infrastructure for k3s migration evaluation.

## Comprehensive Homelab Infrastructure Analysis

Based on thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete breakdown of your homelab infrastructure:

---

## 1. LXC PROVISIONING ARCHITECTURE

### Module Structure (tofu/modules/)

**lxc-base** (foundation layer):
- Uses bpg/proxmox provider (~0.69)
- Creates unprivileged LXC containers by default
- Implements dual-network architecture with dynamic feature configuration
- Supports GPU passthrough via SSH (API token limitations for privileged ops)
- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Network nesting, keyctl, fuse features configurable via `pct set` commands
  - AppArmor profile management (unconfined for privileged containers)
  - Device passthrough for `/dev/dri/card0`, `/dev/renderD128`, `/dev/kfd` (AMD GPU)
  - Lifecycle management with import-friendly ignores

**docker-lxc** (application-focused layer):
- Wraps lxc-base with Docker-specific defaults
- Pre-configured with nesting=true, keyctl=true
- Uses filesync provider for configuration deployment
- Portainer Edge Agent integration (outbound credentials)
- **Deployment Flow:**
  1. LXC creation via lxc-base module
  2. File sync via filesync provider (includes docker-compose.yml)
  3. Optional .env generation for Portainer Edge credentials
  4. SSH-based post-deployment configuration

### Container Features & Security

**Privileged vs Unprivileged:**
- **Privileged (unprivileged=false):**
  - Traefik (200) - requires ports 80/443
  - Network Services (101) - Tailscale, AdGuard DNS on port 53
  - Media Management (402) - requires /dev/net/tun for Gluetun VPN
  
- **Unprivileged (unprivileged=true):**
  - Portainer (100), Dashboards (201), Authelia (202)
  - Jellyfin (401), Immich (304), OpenWebUI (501)
  - Monitoring (500), n8n (502), Obsidian Sync (503), Documents (504)

**GPU Passthrough Configuration:**
- Available for unprivileged containers (OpenWebUI, Jellyfin, Immich)
- Devices: `/dev/dri/card0`, `/dev/dri/renderD128`, `/dev/kfd` (AMD ROCm)
- Cgroup permissions: `lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:* rwm` and `c 234:* rwm`
- GID assignments: gid=44 for /dev/dri/card0, gid=104 for renderD128

---

## 2. DOCKER DEPLOYMENT ACROSS LXCs

### Current Stack (12 Active LXCs)

| LXC ID | Name | IP (Container/LAN) | Status | Services |
|--------|------|-------------------|--------|----------|
| 100 | Portainer | 10.100.1.100 | Unprivileged | Portainer, Watchtower |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Privileged | AdGuard, Cloudflared, Tailscale, DDNS |
| 102 | PBS | 10.100.1.102 | N/A | Proxmox Backup Server (native) |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | Privileged | Traefik (ports 80/443) |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Unprivileged | Homepage, Dashy, Glances |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Unprivileged | Authelia (SSO), Redis |
| 303 | Immich Importer | 10.100.3.103 / 192.168.1.223 | Unprivileged | iCloudPD, photo imports |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Unprivileged | Immich server/ML/DB/Redis (GPU) |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Unprivileged | Jellyfin, Jellyseerr, Jellystat, PostgreSQL (GPU) |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Privileged | Gluetun, qBittorrent, Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, FlareSolverr |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 / 192.168.1.229 | Unprivileged | Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Uptime Kuma, ntfy, OpenTelemetry |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Unprivileged | OpenWebUI, Ollama (AMD GPU, 12 cores, 24GB RAM) |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Unprivileged | n8n workflow automation |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Unprivileged | CouchDB LiveSync |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Unprivileged | Paperless-ngx, Stirling-PDF |

### Deployment Mechanisms

**File Sync Pattern:**
- filesync provider handles docker-compose.yml and configs
- Excludes: migrated-dynamic/*, .env templates
- Post-deployment: manual `docker compose up -d` via SSH (NOT automated)

**Portainer Integration:**
- Edge Agents dial OUT to Portainer (port 8000 on LXC 100)
- Credentials: PORTAINER_EDGE_ID and PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY from 1Password
- All LXCs configured with Edge Agent except Traefik
- No inbound port 9001 exposure (security improvement)

---

## 3. IDENTIFIED PAIN POINTS (from .beads/issues.jsonl)

### Critical Issues (Completed - Dec 14-15)
- **Security:** Image version pinning (40+ containers), InsecureSkipVerify in Traefik, hardcoded passwords
- **Privilege:** Convert 12 LXCs to unprivileged mode (mostly done)
- **Port Access:** Traefik ports 80/443 bind issue on unprivileged containers

### High Priority (OPEN)
1. **Loki Log Aggregation** (755) - No centralized logging; Loki commented out
2. **Container Resource Limits** (u9s) - 88% of services lack memory/CPU limits
3. **Health Checks** (xe3) - 68 of ~80 containers missing healthcheck definitions
4. **Hardcoded IPs** (x4f) - 8 files have hardcoded 192.168.1.x IPs instead of local.lan_ips references

### Recent Infrastructure Epic (OPEN)
- **LXC Infrastructure Stack** (mcd) - New pattern for observability sidecars on all Docker LXCs:
  - Portainer Edge Agent (existing)
  - Diun (image update notifications → ntfy)
  - Node Exporter (host metrics for Prometheus)
  - **Sub-tasks:**
    - Docker Events Notifier (container crash notifications)
    - Remote Docker Compose provider (automate `docker compose up` triggers)

---

## 4. NETWORK TOPOLOGY

### Address Space Design

```
Home LAN:        192.168.1.0/24 (vmbr0)
  └─ FIOS Router:    192.168.1.1
  └─ Proxmox Host:   192.168.1.215
  
Container Net:   10.100.0.0/16 (vmbr1)
  └─ Gateway:        10.100.0.1 (Proxmox vmbr1)
```

### IP Allocation Scheme (Container ID aligned)

```
10.100.1.x    Core services (100-149)
  ├─ 10.100.1.100  Portainer
  ├─ 10.100.1.101  Network Services
  └─ 10.100.1.102  PBS

10.100.2.x    Dashboards & Auth (200-249)
  ├─ 10.100.2.200  Traefik
  ├─ 10.100.2.201  Dashboards
  └─ 10.100.2.202  Authelia

10.100.3.x    Media - Photos (300-349)
  ├─ 10.100.3.103  Immich Importer
  └─ 10.100.3.104  Immich

10.100.4.x    Media - Streaming (400-449)
  ├─ 10.100.4.101  Jellyfin
  └─ 10.100.4.102  Media Management

10.100.5.x    Monitoring & AI (500-549)
  ├─ 10.100.5.100  Monitoring
  ├─ 10.100.5.101  OpenWebUI
  ├─ 10.100.5.102  n8n
  ├─ 10.100.5.103  Obsidian Sync
  └─ 10.100.5.104  Documents
```

### Dual-NIC Services (LAN Access Required)

These services need both container network AND LAN IP for specific capabilities:

| Service | Container IP | LAN IP | Reason |
|---------|--------------|--------|--------|
| Traefik | 10.100.2.200 | 192.168.1.235 | LAN clients access services |
| AdGuard | 10.100.1.101 | 192.168.1.196 | DNS for LAN devices (port 53) |
| Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 | 192.168.1.226 | DLNA/casting to LAN devices |
| Immich | 10.100.3.104 | 192.168.1.222 | Mobile app sync from LAN |
| Immich Importer | 10.100.3.103 | 192.168.1.223 | Photo import processing |

**Network Configuration:**
- eth0 (vmbr1): Container network (required, 10.100.x.x/16)
- eth1 (vmbr0): LAN network (optional for dual-nic services, 192.168.1.x/24)
- eth1 gateway: NULL (avoids routing conflicts with eth0 default route)

---

## 5. GPU PASSTHROUGH CONFIGURATIONS

### Hardware
- **GPU:** AMD Radeon 890M (on Proxmox host)
- **ROCM Support:** Ollama and Immich ML use ROCm for acceleration

### Implementation (lxc-base module)

**Devices Passed:**
```
dev0: /dev/dri/card0 (gid=44)           # GPU device
dev1: /dev/dri/renderD128 (gid=104)     # Render device
dev2: /dev/kfd (no gid)                 # Kernel Fusion Driver
```

**Cgroup Permissions (unprivileged containers):**
```
lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:* rwm  # DRI devices
lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 234:* rwm  # KFD device

Here are the search results for "k3s AMD GPU ROCm device plugin kubernetes 2024":

## Overview

There are several options for enabling AMD GPU support with ROCm in Kubernetes/k3s clusters:

### 1. ROCm k8s-device-plugin

This plugin targets Kubernetes v1.18+ and needs to be run on all nodes equipped with AMD GPU.(no content)The simplest way to deploy it is by creating a Kubernetes DaemonSet. There's a pre-built Docker image on DockerHub and a pre-defined yaml file named `k8s-ds-amdgpu-dp.yaml`.

To install:
```bash
kubectl create -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ROCm/k8s-device-plugin/master/k8s-ds-amdgpu-dp.yaml
```

The latest release (v1.31.0.3) includes updates to address CVE-2024-45339, CVE-2024-45336, and CVE-2024-45341.

### 2. ROCm GPU Operator (Recommended for K3s)

K3s is a lightweight, certified Kubernetes distribution designed for resource-constrained environments. It simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters while maintaining compatibility with standard Kubernetes tools and APIs.(no content)When combined with the ROCm GPU Operator, K3s can efficiently manage AMD GPUs within the cluster, automating tasks such as GPU resource management and monitoring. This allows developers to easily deploy and scale applications that take advantage of AMD GPU acceleration, without the complexity of manual configuration.(no content)The AMD GPU Operator simplifies the deployment and management of AMD Instinct GPU accelerators within Kubernetes clusters, enabling seamless configuration and operation of GPU-accelerated workloads, including machine learning, Generative AI, and other GPU-intensive applications.

**Installation via Helm:**
```bash
helm repo add rocm https://rocm.github.io/gpu-operator
helm repo update

helm install amd-gpu-operator rocm/gpu-operator-charts \
  --namespace kube-amd-gpu \
  --create-namespace \
  --version=v1.4.0
```

This deploys the AMD GPU Operator into the kube-amd-gpu namespace, enabling the management and utilization of AMD GPUs in the Kubernetes cluster.

### 3. Example Setup Guide (2024)

One documented setup uses AMD GPU Instinct MI210 with ROCm 6.0 on Ubuntu 20.04 with Docker 25 and Kubernetes 1.27.

### 4. Node Labeller

The AMD GPU Node Labeller tool automatically labels nodes with GPU properties if a node has one or more AMD GPUs installed.(no content)This enables more precise workload scheduling.

### 5. Minikube Support

As of October 2024, minikube added support for AMD GPU via `--gpu=amd` for docker linux amd64.

### Troubleshooting

If operand pods are stuck in Init:0/1 state, it means your GPU worker doesn't have the inbox GPU driver loaded. You may need to modify the default DeviceConfig to install the out-of-tree GPU driver.(no content)If no operand pods show up, the default DeviceConfig selector `feature.node.kubernetes.io/amd-gpu: "true"` may not find any matched node. If using GPU in a VM, you may need to change the selector to `feature.node.kubernetes.io/amd-vgpu: "true"`.
